Hi Alex — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and requests so we have alignment on the RTBF/delete expectations and how backups/logging interact with those requests.

Call recap (short):
- Scope: patient-identifiable records surfaced by calls to the Redwood hosted inference API (text prompts, outputs, and per-request metadata).
- Requirement: Greenline needs the ability to satisfy individual erasure requests (RTBF) and an audit attestation for each request.
- Residency: majority US, subset of EU patients (we noted dual residency requirements).

Open questions we discussed (please confirm):
1) Target SLA for user-visible purge (you mentioned 30 days). Is acceptable finality 30 days after request?
2) Backups: you asked whether we can purge data from backups or whether backups are immutable.
3) Logs: whether redaction of PII in request/response logs is sufficient, or Greenline requires complete deletion from all logging systems.

What I attached: Greenline_Audit_Questions.xlsx — I filled the columns we covered today so we can iterate.

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm (1)-(3) above and add any required legal/format constraints.
- If you still need a faster SLA for backup removal, we can scope Dedicated/Private options where we can alter backup retention/rotation and provide stronger attestation.
- I'll schedule a 45-minute technical deep dive with Marissa (Privacy Ops) and Ben (SRE/SE) to walk through the operational steps and produce a simple MAP (mutual action plan).

Thanks — Jonas

Thanks Jonas — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) SLA: Greenline would prefer user-visible deletion within 30 days. Ideally we'd have an option to accelerate to 7 days for high-risk patient data, but 30 days is our baseline.
2) Backups: our legal team wants backups to be scrubbed within 90 days where feasible. We understand some immutable snapshot systems make immediate removal challenging; we need a documented approach that results in eventual removal and an attestation we can include in our compliance package.
3) Logs: we prefer full deletion, but if the engineering complexity is high, redaction (hashing/field removal) combined with limited retention would be acceptable — as long as we can prove PII is not recoverable and have an audit trail of the deletion action.

I'm attaching our internal policy excerpt that shows categories of data we consider PII and a short checklist for our legal reviewers (Greenline_Internal_Policy.docx).

Also: can you point me to Redwood's SOC2 summary and any existing DPA language that supports a 30-day user purge + 90-day backup scrub?

If you can draft a one-pager showing the operational steps that happen after we submit an RTBF request (who does what, expected timing window, what we can attest to), that would help us move this through our procurement team faster.

Appreciate it — Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear responses and the policy excerpt. High-level answers below; Ben/Marissa will add technical details and residency notes.

User-visible purge (30 days):
- Hosted: we can remove all tenant/customer data from active stores within 30 days. We will return an attestation indicating the request id and timestamp of completion.
- Dedicated/Private: we can support accelerated timelines (7–14 days) because we can change snapshot/retention policies on the customer pool.

Backups:
- Hosted offering: our standard backup rotation creates immutable snapshots that we keep per policy. Practically we cannot instantly edit an immutable snapshot; instead we guarantee logical deletion from the service and we schedule scrub-on-rotation. For example, if our rotation is 90 days, after the next rotation the data will no longer be present. We can also provide a signed attestation that the item was marked deleted on X date and removed from active indices.
- For customers needing a contractual 90-day scrub window, we can either: (a) move to a Dedicated pool with a modified retention schedule, or (b) agree to a documented process for hosted that provides the attestation plus a timeline tied to snapshot retention.

Logs:
- We can redact request/response text from logs on request, and we can optionally keep aggregated, non-reversible telemetry for metrics. Raw request logs are retained for debugging for 30 days by default; we can shorten that window for Dedicated/Private offerings.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Marissa will draft an RTBF operational one-pager that shows the end-to-end steps and the artifacts (attestations) you receive.
2) Ben will prepare a short technical appendix showing where data is stored, backup cadence, and the expected timeline for removal from backups.
3) I'll prepare a DPA excerpt that captures the 30-day purge baseline and options for a 90-day backup scrub for your legal team to review.

I'll attach our RTBF workflow doc to give you an operational picture.

Best — Jonas

Subject: Technical appendix: retention, backups, and logs (short)

Alex — adding the technical view you asked for so procurement has concrete steps. TL;DR: active removal is fast; backups and low-level storage depend on the retention window.

Operational sequence when an RTBF request is received (high level):
- Inbound: request submitted to Privacy Ops portal (or via API) -> ticket created.
- Active store deletion: service executes a deletion job that removes references from primary indices and KV stores (T+0 to T+48h depending on load).
- Cache & in-memory: KV caches and node-local stores are invalidated immediately after job completion.
- Snapshots/backups: snapshots are immutable; logical deletion flags are applied to the customer namespace immediately. Actual binary removal occurs on the next snapshot rotation/GC pass. Typical rotation window for hosted snapshots is 60–120 days depending on region — default is 90 days.
- For Dedicated/Private: we can change snapshot/backup rotation to meet contractual windows (e.g., 30/45/90 days) and run a targeted purge during a maintenance window if required.

Logging specifics:
- Request/response logs retained in plaintext for 30 days; after 30 days we either purge or aggregate (per contract).
- Audit logs (who/when) are kept for 365 days by default; those can be shortened but we keep an immutable record of the deletion action for compliance evidence.

Attachments: redwood-retention-config-sample.yaml (example config you can use to scope Dedicated). Also linking a short Drive doc with SOC/controls.

If you confirm Greenline wants the 30-day user purge + 90-day backup scrub as a contract clause, we will draft language and outline the technical changes for Dedicated vs Hosted.
